title: SE Bootcamp: 30min Technical Sprint Outline
body:
Purpose:
Run a focused, repeatable 30-minute technical sprint that an SE can run with an integration architect or platform engineer. The goal is to surface a) immediate feasibility for a pilot, b) rough performance/cost expectations, and c) obvious blockers (network, auth, model choice). This is a running template — use the script, tweak timing per customer.

Audience:
- Integration architects, platform engineers, senior backend engineers evaluating Redwood inference for low-latency / predictable-throughput use cases
- Timeboxed: 30 minutes (strict)

Outcome (measurable):
- Pilot go/no-go decision within 30 minutes with next steps
- Collect 3 signal metrics: 1) median p50 latency for 128-token generation, 2) tokens/sec throughput on a 1 RPS simulated burst, 3) first-pass cost per 1k tokens estimate using our unit rates
- Capture blockers as Jira epics or risks list

Pre-call prep (SE) — 15–30 min before session:
- Confirm customer's preferred model family and sample request types (chat / completion / embeddings) via Slack/Email
- Prepare a short prompt set (3 items): one simple generation, one long-context with instruction, one embedding/retrieval test
- Ensure demo account has API key and Quiet Mode on (no billing surprises)
- Provision a shared Postman collection and a single test script (curl + sample prompt) — link in calendar invite
- Open the Live Console and pre-load the model variant recommended for the use case (e.g., 4-bit quantized variant for cost-sensitive demo)

30-minute runbook (timeline + script):
- 0:00–2:00 — Quick intros and framing (SE + customer)
  - Confirm goals of the sprint (latency vs. cost vs. accuracy). Call out SLO expectations.
  - Ask: production target concurrency, average prompt length, and PII/compliance concerns. 

- 2:00–6:00 — Walkthrough of Redwood runtime architecture (2 slides, 4 min)
  - One-slide: routing & fallback policy (region, capacity tier, model variant)
  - One-slide: caching & batching basics (prefix caching, KV cache re-use)
  - Quick pointer to Console > Traces and Token-level cost panel for later exploration

- 6:00–12:00 — Live API call walkthrough (SE drives)
  - Run the prepped simple generation (show raw request + response streaming)
  - Show Console live trace for that single request (highlight cold vs warm KV cache traces if possible)
  - Capture p50 latency from trace and annotate in shared doc

- 12:00–18:00 — Throughput & burst simulation (SE or customer runs)
  - Use the included script to simulate a 1 RPS then a 10 RPS short burst (30s). Watch autoscaling/queueing behavior in Console.
  - Note throughput, any queuing, and fallback triggers. If using Dedicated plan demo, show reserved pool metrics.
  - Record tokens/sec and any observed variance (put into quick table).

- 18:00–24:00 — Cost & quality tradeoff quick exploration
  - Swap model variant (e.g., base -> quantized) and re-run the simple generation to collect new latency and token cost delta.
  - If time, show an embedding call and estimate embedding cost per 1k vectors.
  - Pull the Console cost panel to get an immediate estimate.

- 24:00–28:00 — Risk checklist + blocker capture (SE asks the customer for answers)
  - Network constraints (firewalls, egress limits, VPC peering needs)
  - Data residency & logging concerns (do they need Private deployment?)
  - Auth & key management (KMS/HSM requirement?)
  - Integration complexity (batching at client vs server-side, pre/post-processing)

- 28:00–30:00 — Decision and next steps
  - SE states recommendation: pilot (yes/no/conditional). If yes: propose pilot scope (2–4 week, model variant, target KPIs), owner, and required resources.
  - Assign Jira ticket for pilot kickoff and mark any immediate blockers as epics.

Demo artifacts to attach to post-call notes:
- Prompts used (canonical set)
- p50/p95 latency measured, tokens/sec, estimated cost per 1k tokens for each variant tested
- Screenshot of Console trace and cost panel, plus link to snippet in shared Postman collection

Quick reference scripts (to paste into terminal during the demo):
- curl sample for generation (with streaming header)
- small python snippet to run 30s burst with concurrency using httpx/async
- quick jq commands to extract token counts and latency from trace JSON
(links to scripts: github.com/redwood-inference/demo-scripts/bootcamp-30min)

Success criteria for green pilot: (use as checklist)
- Median latency target met for the primary flow (customer-defined)
- No infra-level blockers (network/auth) unresolved
- Pilot owner assigned and contract/credits allocated (if hosted)

Common objections and SE quick responses (scripts):
- "Latency is too high for us" -> Ask for typical prompt length, offer quantized variant or dedicated pool, propose edge routing and prefix caching follow-up to shave cold-starts
- "Costs unknown" -> Run the quick cost delta matrix live (base vs quantized) and commit to a post-pilot cost report; propose Optimize recommendations after 1k calls
- "We need on-prem or VPC" -> Capture regulatory need, propose Private deployment assessment and intro to Solutions Eng if > enterprise scope

Hand-offs and post-call tasks (SE):
- Create Pilot Jira with: scope, target KPIs, pilot owner, duration, and resources needed
- Upload screenshots and quantitative results to the Jira ticket and link back to Confluence onboarding template
- Slack ping to Solutions Eng (if Private deployment likely) with exec summary and link to artifacts

Notes to SE-runner (best practices):
- Timebox strictly — customers respect short, concrete outcomes. If technical deep-dive appears needed, schedule follow-up longer working session.
- Try to switch model variants early (within first 12 minutes) so the customer sees tradeoffs
- Keep one eye on cost panel during bursts; noisy customers can inflate demo costs quickly
- Save all traces and tag them with the customer name in Console for easy retrieval (trace metadata: customer:<name>, sprint:30min)

Appendix: Troubleshooting ticks
- No responses: check API key, region mismatch, model unavailable -> swap to fallback variant and retry
- Autoscale not triggering: confirm pool limits and quota on the demo account; if using Dedicated mock, clarify reserved pool settings
- Streaming partial responses: inspect chunk size header and client-side buffer settings

Appendix B: Quick copy for calendar invite (short):
"30-min technical sprint: quick feasibility, latency & cost signals, and pilot recommendation. Bring an architect or SE. We'll run live calls and capture baseline metrics. Please share your target concurrency and a sample prompt ahead of time."

Internal links & references:
- Onramp template (Confluence): CONFLUENCE-RT-INFERENCE-ONRAMP
- Demo scripts repo: github.com/redwood-inference/demo-scripts/bootcamp-30min
- Pilot kickoff ticket template: JIRA-GTM-8521

Last edited by: Maya Singh — remember to add any local region-specific notes before running (EU GDPR customers: default to Private assessment threshold at pilot stage).
